text:
alex: Heads-up — after the 11:30 canary deploy (runtime v2.14.0) I'm seeing p99 regression on text-gen routes: from ~200ms -> ~420ms. p95 also moved. Canary traffic is tiny but spike is consistent across a few hosts.

infra-bot: deploy v2.14.0 completed on canary group (canary-03).

maya: confirmed on observability: p50 20ms p95 110ms p99 420ms on canary-03. non-canary hosts steady.

samir: what changed in v2.14.0? I skimmed the PR: dynamic microbatch heuristic + kernel selector update (prefer fused_attn_v2 on compatible GPUs) + kvcache sharding tweak.

devon: microbatch heuristic now increases batch target to 32 for low-concurrency long-tail workloads — meant to boost throughput. Could be oversizing for short sequences.

alex: I ran a quick local profiler on canary-03. Flame shows big tail in attention kernel when batch size >= 16 and seq_len <= 64. Kernel selection picks fused_attn_v2 which is faster for long seqs but regresses on small seqs under high variance.

maya: snippet from quick profile: 
```
latency_histogram_ms: {p50: 18, p95: 120, p99: 420}
top_stack: fused_attn_v2::forward -> kv_cache::lookup -> runtime::dispatch
```

samir: also seeing increased KV cache miss amplification after the sharding tweak — more small cache misses that trigger recompute paths. Miss rate up from 1.1% -> 3.8% on canary.

devon: putting pieces together: dynamic microbatch pushes to larger microbatches -> kernel selector picks fused_attn_v2 for throughput -> on short sequences fused_attn_v2 has worse variance -> combined with extra KV-cache misses we get tail amplification.

maya: can we force the kernel selector back to the previous policy (fallback to fused_attn_v1 for seq<=64) as a rollback step without reverting the whole deploy?

alex: yes we have a kernel_selection override flag in /etc/redwood/runtime/config.d/kernel-override.yaml. Can flip to "prefer_v1_for_short_seq: true".

deploy-bot: starting config change: kernel-override.yaml -> prefer_v1_for_short_seq: true (target: canary-03).

infra-bot: applied kernel-override on canary-03 hosts.

maya: monitoring... p99 dropping on canary-03 to ~190ms within 45s. p95 back to ~90ms. Good signal.

samir: but KV miss rate still elevated. Need follow-up on sharding tweak — reverting that might require full rollback. Miss-rate steady ~3.6%.

devon: agree, kernel override buys time. Suggest we revert microbatch heuristic too — it's a config toggle: microbatch.max_target default 32, revert to 8. That should reduce both kernel pressure and working set for kvcache.

alex: opinion: do incremental: 1) keep kernel override, 2) set microbatch.max_target: 8 on canary, 3) watch for 5m, then decide on sharding revert. 4) If still bad -> full rollback to v2.13.9.

sre-oncall: ACK. I'll own the change window, prepare rollback steps.

deploy-bot: applying config change microbatch.max_target -> 8 on canary-03 now.

infra-bot: applied microbatch config on canary-03.

maya: p99 now stable ~175-200ms. KV miss rate remains ~3.4% but tail looks acceptable.

alex: rolling decision: pause global rollout, keep v2.14.0 canaries patched with kernel override + microbatch cap, open a follow-up to revert kvcache sharding in next patch.

samir: I'll file a perf regression PR with reproducer and perf traces (will include short-seq fused_attn_v2 bench). Need to add unit tests in kernel selector for seq_len boundary.

devon: we should add a safety check in the heuristic: if model_seq_median < 80 then cap microbatch at 8. I'll draft a change.

alex: thanks everyone. SRE: please monitor for 30m and if stable start canary promotion with the two config protections. We'll run a postmortem tomorrow with profiling artifacts.

sre-oncall: monitoring. if anything flips I'll trigger full rollback to v2.13.9 (rollback playbook link: https://redwood/internal/playbooks/rollback). :white_check_mark:

alex: quick note for postmortem: include kernel perf counters, kvcache miss traces, and a timeline of selector + heuristic changes per commit.

maya: copying logs to #incidents and opening a follow-up ticket: INF-5297 (perf regression: fused_attn_v2 + microbatch heuristic).

alex: thanks — good rapid containment. We'll schedule a deeper runbook review to avoid selector regressions slipping through canaries. :thumbsup:
